pages.text: Delali’s grandfather, Togbe Kwami, farmed maize behind the house. ‘The rains feel late this year,’ he said. ‘But feelings are not the same as numbers.’
sentences: Delali’s grandfather, Togbe Kwami, farmed maize behind the house.

‘But feelings are not the same as numbers.’
pages.alt: An old farmer and a girl stand beside a maize field under a cloudy sky.

pages.text: At school, Madam Rukaya gave each pair a clear plastic bottle with straight sides, with the top cut off by the teacher. Delali turned the top upside down to make a funnel, and taped a ruler to the side with zero at the water level on the flat base.

pages.alt: Children assemble rain gauges from plastic bottles at a classroom table.

pages.text: Delali placed her gauge in an open space away from roofs and trees. Every morning at 8 o’clock she read the water level in millimetres and wrote it in her table. Then she emptied it.

pages.alt: A girl reads a bottle rain gauge in an open yard and writes in a notebook.

pages.text: After one week her table said: Monday 0 mm, Tuesday 12 mm, Wednesday 0 mm, Thursday 0 mm, Friday 5 mm, Saturday 0 mm, Sunday 0 mm. Total: 17 mm.

Total: 17 mm.
pages.alt: A notebook page shows a week-long table of rainfall in millimetres.

pages.text: Selorm’s gauge said only 7 mm on Tuesday. ‘One of us must be wrong,’ he said. ‘Or both of us,’ said Delali. They did not argue. They went to look at both gauges together.
sentences: Selorm’s gauge said only 7 mm on Tuesday.

pages.text: Selorm’s gauge stood under a mango tree. Leaves and branches had caught some of the rain. ‘The tree took my rain!’ he laughed. He moved his gauge to the open yard, and the next readings matched Delali’s within 1 mm.

pages.alt: A bottle gauge sits under a mango tree, then is moved into the open yard.

pages.text: Delali told her grandfather, ‘One millimetre of rain means one litre of water on every square metre of ground. So 17 mm is 17 litres on each square metre of your field.’ Togbe Kwami whistled. ‘That is real evidence.’

pages.text: Togbe Kwami kept the table. ‘Next year I will compare it,’ he said. Delali smiled. One week of data could not answer every question about the weather, but it was a good start. The end.

activities.question: What was the total rainfall in Delali’s first week?

activities.prompt: Selorm’s reading was lower than Delali’s. Why might two gauges in the same town give different readings?
options: One was blocked by a tree
Rain falls differently on different days of the week

activities.question: Why was Selorm’s gauge giving a lower reading?
options: Leaves and branches caught some rain
He read it at the wrong time
